exposure: Prolonged second stage of labor (≥3 hours of pushing)
cohort: 1465 nulliparous women with term, singleton, and vertex pregnancies who received midwifery-led care at a single academic center in the United States
finding: In nulliparous individuals with prolonged second stage of labor, fetal malposition, epidural analgesia, and longer passive descent were associated with cesarean birth and OASI, but not with PPH or poor neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Prolonged pushing, epidural analgesia, and longer passive descent were associated with cesarean birth and OASI in nulliparous individuals.
